intros.intro: Mosslit Wood begins at an old boardwalk. Ferns reach under fallen trunks. Mushrooms grow on shaded stone. Where the stream bends, pebbles show.
Amber Hollow is warmer than outside. Warm crystals sit in the rock. An underground stream slips past the spikes. Drops fall into a shallow pool.
Cloudreach steps float in the wind. A broken bridge hangs in the air, its banner pulled straight. Gardens sit on floating islands. Birds pass above.
Lilywater Court is flat. Lilies open on the surface, and lily pads step across. Ripples blur the pavilion's reflection. Coral grows in the shallows.
Starscript Hall is rune tiles and star murals. Crystal pillars drop patches of light on the floor. Bronze rings sit in the stone. Stardust hangs low.

blessings.blessing: When moss grows out of the crack, light rests on the underside of the leaf for a while.
Warmth moves slowly in the cave, and moss in the cracks still remembers the old light.
The cloud steps hold a foot, and the wind carries light things to the other side.
When the shell opens and closes, the light underwater shifts.
Stardust settles lightly, and light patches in the corridor keep a place for each step.

lines: Water light in the walk seams.
The fern glows near three lights.
The log's mushrooms are whiter.
The hollow's light looks wrapped.
Did you hear water under leaves?
Same path. The moss is thicker.
One tap tells if a step is loose.
Gate ferns lean toward the water.
Mossy fork stones are drier.
I rest here. I will still be here.
Cave water outlives the stone.
My moss grows thick while I sit.
Crystal glow shows wall lines.
Amber light is old, still warm.
Do the drops land in one spot?
Three ways. Low vines are easier.
Firm where the stick has tested.
Stream sound is clearer than wind.
Warm stone feels like sunlit wall.
You came this way for the amber?
Wind rises through the step gap.
I stop at that gap on mail runs.
Old rope swings at the bridge end.
Soil is thin, but roots hold on.
Can you tell a step from a cloud?
Steps feel firm but look fragile.
Light stick. I stow it in wind.
Flowers on the isle grow thicker.
All cloud below; no shadow falls.
Less wind. The stick lands firm.
Ripples reach the edge and ebb.
I open slowly. The light lags.
Roots in mud. The flower floats.
Reflections break, then close.
Did you see pale green dots below?
Two sunken steps still sound.
Stick in water tells the pad edge.
Wood above the water stays dry.
Ripples make the coral below sway.
Did you hear the eave drops?
Silver dust fills the brick seams.
Sat long. Moss climbs to my knees.
Wall arcs are paler than runes.
Ring turns draw a little wind.
Did the light patch hold one side?
Wide entrance. Sound thins inside.
Two taps, and the echoes differ.
Pillar light patches are brighter.
Mural dots break off at the ring.
Did the tooth turn to the light?

levels: The side door light stays dark.
The lamp lights only under weight.
Rock on the switch keeps the door up.
The crystal seat is still dark.
A mirror block in the beam bends it.
A mirror turns the beam to the seat.
The tiles by the stone door stay still.
Three pads take the mural order.
Three pads in order open the stone door.
The next floating platform is far away.
Side wind pushes the platform forward.
Wait in the updraft, then jump across.
The platform ahead has not risen.
The wheel can turn the flow another way.
Gate open, water rises, platform floats.
The frame pattern still lacks a corner.
Pieces lie in the hall and wall niches.
Three pieces make the frame whole again.

gallery.title: First Road in Rain
gallery.caption: Rain on his hood. Dry crust in the satchel. The boardwalk is long. He does not look back.

gallery.title: Sitting in the Dark
gallery.caption: He learns to sit in the dark and count time by drops until light reaches his feet.

gallery.title: Lifted by the Wind
gallery.caption: The wind lifts him off the ground. He sees the landing place ahead, not underfoot.

gallery.title: Water to the Knees
gallery.caption: Water to the knees. No way back. He lifts the satchel and walks toward the louder water.

gallery.title: One Line of Light
gallery.caption: Five crystals make one line. The Stillwater Veil never stopped him. It only slowed him.

story: He left with nothing, wanting to see the far side. Rain on his hood, one dry crust. In the caves he learned to wait; in the wind, to trust his eyes; in the water, to let the way back go; in the hall, to look behind. When five crystals made one line he understood: the Stillwater Veil was never a wall, only a reason to finish the walk. The far side was not as he imagined. It was a little brighter.
